newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Active Australian stocks slide to lower close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Active Australian stocks slide to lower close.

text.p: An active Australian sharemarket slid to a lower close on Wednesday, the market following the Dow down early and quickly settling in about 10 points lower.
At 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 9.4 points lower at 2,370.7. December share price index futures were six points lower at 2,380, a 9.3 point premium to the index.
While the day's end result showed a loss, brokers were heartened by the local bourse's relatively muted response to Wall Street's 1.2 percent loss.
Turnover topped A$1.2 billion, reflecting what brokers said was a surprisingly active day with solid investor interest.
"It was a very good performance. Everyone was expecting a much duller day than it hasturned out to be," said broker Kevin Lourey of Peake Lands Kirwan.
Topping turnover was ANZ Bank with its attractive dividend yield seen as the lure for buyers despite previous takeover speculation.
"I believe it is the yield. There is perennial talk of ANZ being in line for takeover, but that won't happen until Wallis has reported."
The Federal government-appointed Wallis inquiry into the financial system is due to conclude in March 1997.

Other stocks under the spotlight included oil and gas explorer, Bligh Oil and Minerals, whose scrip soared 48 percent to A$0.51, their highest level in nearly seven years, as traders digested Tuesday's report of the discovery of a major gas zone in its exploration areas in Texas.

On the downside, shares in Perth-based computer group Formulab Neuronetics slumped as profit takers, tempted by the strong gains of the last month, cashed in after the U.S. launch of the Richter Paradigm Computer.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about seven to five, while about 27 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivatives saw a pickup in activity in line with the strong turnover seen in underlying markets.
Total options traded 40,670 (30,484)
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 7,682 (5,209)
In other local markets, the Australian dollar was in a daze Wednesday after suffering its biggest fall in a decade.
Traders said an orderly correction dissolved into rout offshore Tuesday when the market reacted badly to loose talk of lower interest rates and stripped it of almost three cents.
The fall, however, was seen as a heaven sent opportunity by local exporters and funds desperate to take forex cover.
By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT) the currency was trying to find its feet at US$0.7974/79 having bounced from a deep offshore low of US$0.7855, but was still far below Tuesday's late US$0.8135/40.
In the Australian bond markets, the price action in the last 24 hours has led some analysts to believe the rally since September has finally run its course.
While the 10-year bond yield finally made a push below 7.0 percent in after hours trading, the move met a solid rejection, and coincided with a slide in the Australian dollar.
By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), the 10 year Treasury bonds were yielding 7.095 percent.
